text: You've played games forever. Jumping, moving, attacking – it's second nature. You just downloaded a new game, ready for action.
But the game starts, and a pop-up screams: 'Press X to Jump!' You scoff. Of course you know how to jump! What an annoying interruption.
You wonder if developers think you're clueless, or if it's bad design. This feels like an unnecessary, frustrating hurdle before the real fun.
The system isn't insulting you. These basic tutorials aren't just for pros, but for *everyone* – the new, the tired, the distracted player.
By ensuring every player can perform basic actions, the game minimizes early frustration. This crucial onboarding maximizes engagement and retention.
Next time a game tells you to move forward, you'll still roll your eyes. But you'll see the invisible system ensuring millions more players stay on the journey.
